deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous pages). X is a space with a locally finite family (X_i), i in a poset I, of closed subspaces. The conditions (21 a-d) say roughly the following:
- i <= j implies X_i is contained in X_j;
- the X_i cover X;
- X_i ∩ X_j is the union of the X_k with k <= i, j.

For x in X, I_x = {i : x ∈ X_i} is finite and decreasingly filtered, so it has a least element i(x) (25).

This page, (26). Put Ẋ_i = ∪_{j<i} X_j. This is closed in X_i by local finiteness and is the 'boundary' of X_i. Put X_i^* = X_i \ Ẋ_i, open in X_i, the 'open stratum'.

Proposition. The X_i^* are pairwise disjoint and cover X. For each x, i(x) is the unique i with x ∈ X_i^*.

Proof.
- Disjointness: suppose x ∈ X_i^* ∩ X_j^* with i ≠ j. By (21 d) there is k <= i, j with x ∈ X_k.
  - If k = i, then i < j, so x ∈ X_i ⊂ Ẋ_j, contradicting x ∈ X_j^*.
  - The case k = j is symmetric.
  - So k < i, hence x ∈ X_k ⊂ Ẋ_i, contradicting x ∈ X_i^*.
- Covering: x ∈ X_{i(x)}^* by minimality of i(x).

Thus the closed filtered cover is converted into a partition of X into locally closed strata indexed by I. A margin NB notes:
- empty X_i are allowed;
- restricting to I' = {i : X_i^* ≠ ∅} still satisfies conditions (21 a-d).

(27)-(28). These pass to the simplicial space X_{Δ_•} built earlier. Presumably X_{Δ_r} is a coproduct over chains i_0 <= … <= i_r of copies of X_{i_0} (a nerve-type simplicial resolution of X by its closed pieces), with σ_r : X_{Δ_r} → X_{Δ_0} induced by the vertex 0. Then:
- Ẋ_{Δ_0} = ∐ Ẋ_i and X^*_{Δ_0} = ∐ X_i^*;
- for every r, Ẋ_{Δ_r} and X^*_{Δ_r} are defined as inverse images under σ_r. They form a closed 'singular/boundary' part and an open 'nonsingular' part of each X_{Δ_r}.

The next page checks these are stable under simplicial operators α with α(0) = 0. The stated aim is to reconstruct X from the open strata X_i^* plus gluing data, generalizing n°1 (two strata Y ⊂ X with a tubular-type U_{Y,X}). This is the start of Grothendieck's 'stratified topos' / dévissage programme.
errors: Minor: the disjointness proof treats only k = i explicitly; the case k = j is symmetric and omitted.

The justification 'absurde car x ∈ X_j^* = X_j \ X_i^*' as transcribed is wrong as written. The correct reason is X_i ⊂ Ẋ_j when i < j, so x ∉ X_j^*. Grothendieck's handwriting is probably a slip or ambiguous rather than a mathematical error.
Similarly 'x ∈ X_i \ X_k ... contredit x ∈ X_i^*' should read x ∈ X_k ⊂ Ẋ_i.

ideas.what: Passing from a locally finite, poset-indexed family of closed subsets, closed under intersection up to unions, to a partition into locally closed strata X_i^* = X_i \ ∪_{j<i} X_j, with i(x) the least index containing x.
ideas.modern_name: Stratification by a poset; strata of a closed filtration; the stratification map X → I (Alexandrov topology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Whitney, Thom, Mather; poset-stratified spaces in Lurie HA A.5 and Ayala–Francis–Tanaka)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 discusses 'théorie de dévissage des structures stratifiées' informally; no such explicit proposition known to me

ideas.what: Simplicial space X_{Δ_•} (nerve-type resolution indexed by chains in I), with the boundary Ẋ and open part X^* pulled back along the 0-th vertex map, and stability under operators fixing 0.
ideas.modern_name: Décalage / nerve of a closed cover indexed by a poset; homotopy-colimit presentation of a stratified space; precursor of exit-path / link data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Exit-path and stratified homotopy: MacPherson, Treumann (2009), Lurie (HA A.6); décalage: Illusie, Deligne
ideas.where_published: Programme only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out an elementary, correct set-theoretic step: partitioning a closed filtered cover into open strata and transporting it to a simplicial resolution. It is a building block of the larger (interesting) stratified-reconstruction programme, but nothing on this page itself goes beyond standard material.
transcription_corrections: Margin NB reads roughly: 'NB On n'exclut pas que des X_i soient = ∅ (si on l'exclut il faut supposer X_i ≠ ∅ ...); si I' ⊂ I ensemble des i ∈ I tels que X_i^* ≠ ∅, (X_i)_{i∈I'} satisfait encore les conditions (21 a) à d)'.
'X_j^* = X_j \ X_i^*' is better read as X_j^* = X_j \ Ẋ_j, i.e. ⊂ X_j \ X_i.
'x ∈ X_i \ X_k' likely means x ∈ X_k ⊂ Ẋ_i, i.e. x ∉ X_i^*.
Under (28), first line, the annotation is 'fermé de X_{Δ_r}' (partially cut off at the right edge); the second line has 'ouvert de X_{Δ_r}' underneath.
